criteria.criterion: Verified human identities and tenant memberships must be distinct from a Stripe account authorization; operator, production customer, product administrator and developer roles require explicit, current server-checked memberships.
criteria.evidence: Tenancy identities and tenant memberships remain isolated by context, role and revision from merged PR #289. This continuation binds encrypted credential AAD to immutable person/tenant/context and exact owned grant, preserving the requirement that actual OIDC proof must be independently implemented before public enrollment.

criteria.criterion: Typed Stripe account/Connect/organization grants must bind tenant, stable person, verified provider account, mode, issuer/resource, permission revision and credential kind, with no cross-tenant credential or operation fallback.
criteria.evidence: Existing grant descriptors have exact selected account/mode/kind and only pending status; the new sealed table and vault require matching persisted principal, membership revision and owned grant. A wrong context/key/tenant cannot decrypt. No actual provider grant can execute; original source permissions remain unknown.

criteria.criterion: Grant enrollment, ownership changes, revocation, replacement, expiry and concurrent use must be atomic and fail closed, without exposing provider bearer secrets or authorizing provider I/O based on metadata alone.
criteria.evidence: New keyless metadata-only operations atomically INSERT once, rotate under expected generation CAS, and revoke without resurrection. AES-GCM envelope and AAD use the existing reviewed crypto, never returned by public tooling. Real PostgreSQL concurrent CAS/revocation tests added. External provider refresh/revoke remain unfinished.

criteria.criterion: Legacy owner-managed accounts/OAuth connections must remain compatible but unassigned; ownership migration requires independently proven owner identity, and ambiguous credentials must never become customer grants.
criteria.evidence: Existing legacy account/AAD/OAuth records are unchanged and not auto-migrated. Tenant schema remains behind the explicit unenabled production migration flag; this PR adds only an inactive table and internal store methods, no LIVE activation or customer mutation.

criteria.criterion: Use disposable real PostgreSQL tests for independent identities, two tenants, same person different roles, foreign account/mode, stale membership, concurrent revocation, and negative provider-authority assumptions; keep signed-in independent money-out approval and LIVE safeguards unchanged.
criteria.evidence: Seven new real disposable PostgreSQL test cases exercise encrypted at-rest material, wrong AAD and key kind/mode, exact owner/account scope, concurrent replace and revocation, absence of plaintext in outputs and stale membership. External mobile/provider acceptance and independent money-out proof remain open and original financial controls unchanged.

Complete the branded one-screen mobile ChatGPT/Claude sign-in and actual consent handback, tenant-bound MCP token issuance/refresh/revocation and existing owner credential migration.

Enable provider-backed verified grant activation and operation-specific permission/entitlement resolver with no credential widening; prove actual provider before/after Full and optional God Mode behavior.
Independent real multi-user/client/provider acceptance for all supported direct and indirect doors, preserving every signed-in money-out and LIVE constraint.

newEngineering: Additive gated encrypted provider-grant vault with AES-256-GCM AAD ownership, atomic pending ciphertext insert, generation-checked rotation, independent metadata-only read and one-time revocation, seven genuine isolated PostgreSQL concurrency/security fixtures and updated migration notes. Codex review fix adds a current-membership exact grant-id lookup and a 105-newer-grant real PostgreSQL regression to prevent capped-list authorization/credential-revocation failures.
planComparison: Delivered 232 new source lines (one replaced) versus estimated 480. This is one coherent security boundary and remains only partial CAP-3 source: provider identity enrollment, verified OAuth grants, tenant-authorized MCP tokens and provider-backed real acceptance cannot be safely conflated with inactive encrypted storage. No CAP-3 subsection completion is credited.
